title: King Street — March 5, 1770
design_note: The game's opening scene, built strictly from Rex v. Preston / Rex v. Wemms testimony. The scene never shows who said 'Fire' — the sources genuinely disagree, and honoring that ambiguity IS the scene (docs/05). Natural light only: first-quarter moon, one sentry's post, falling snow.

events.note: wind, harbor ice, a dog far off

events.text: Five thousand soldiers quartered on a town of sixteen thousand, two years now. Tonight the moon is a quarter full, and there is ice in the streets.
A single sentry of the 29th Regiment stands his post before the Custom House on King Street.
"There were a parcel of boys around the sentry... calling him names, daring him to fire."
Church bells begin to ring across the town — the alarm for FIRE. Boston pours into the street carrying buckets.
There is no fire. The bells themselves are the ambiguity: half the street has come to help, and no one can say afterward what the other half came for.
Captain Thomas Preston and seven men push through the crowd to the sentry — bayonets fixed, muskets loaded.
"Are the men loaded?" — "Yes." — "Are they going to fire?" — "They cannot, without my orders."
events.attribution: Capt. Preston to a townsman, per his deposition

events.text: Snowballs. Oyster shells. Chunks of ice. A thrown club, sworn to by a dozen witnesses.
Private Hugh Montgomery is struck and knocked from his feet. He rises.
No order to fire was ever proven — not by the Crown, not by the town, not by the court. The word 'fire' was in the air; the bells had put it there.
Seven seconds of smoke and silence before anyone understands what has happened.
Crispus Attucks — sailor, of Native and African blood, first to fall — lies dead in the snow. Four more are dead or dying.
"Facts are stubborn things; and whatever may be our wishes, our inclinations, or the dictates of our passions, they cannot alter the state of facts and evidence."
events.attribution: John Adams — counsel for the DEFENSE of these soldiers — Rex v. Wemms, 1770
an American game of the Revolution
